relations.note: Agreed by every source read: the store FAQ (Printing Tips › 1.Accessory Compatibility) "Not compatible with Hotend with Stainless Steel Nozzle 0.2 mm."; the TDS Basic Info (p.1) "it is not recommended to use a 0.2 mm nozzle for printing as clogging may occur"; the TDS Nozzle Size row lists only 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 mm; the PLA wiki "PLA Marble⚠️ ... are not compatible with 0.2 mm stainless steel nozzles"; the material-table wiki row "PLA Marble" gives "Not Compatible" for the 0.2 mm nozzle. compat-targets.json reviews "0.2 mm Nozzle" as unresolvable (component_concept_not_a_product), so no target handle is named.

relations.source_title: Bambu Filament Technical Data Sheet V3.0: PLA Marble
relations.locator: p.1, Recommended Printing Settings › Nozzle Size
relations.note: The material-table wiki row "PLA Marble" gives "Compatible" for the 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8 mm nozzles and the 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8 mm high flow nozzles; the PLA wiki says "All standard nozzles are acceptable (excluding 0.2 mm nozzle)".
relations.conflict: The material-table wiki contradicts itself on the nozzle material: its row "PLA Marble" says hardened steel is "Not Required", while the text under the same table names PLA Marble among particle-filled materials and says "Do not use a stainless steel or brass nozzle", "Always use a hardened steel nozzle" and that "a 0.4 mm hardened steel nozzle is highly recommended as the first choice". The TDS and the store page name no nozzle material. Left to review.

documents.title: Bambu Filament Technical Data Sheet V3.0: PLA Marble
Bambu PLA Marble Safety Data Sheet SDS20251127A07
Bambu Lab Filament Hex Code Table: PLA Marble
Filament guide: printer, nozzle, AMS, build plate and glue compatibility

notes: Mechanical keys hold the TDS X-Y printed-specimen values; the registry has one key per scope, so the Z values (tensile 30 ± 4 MPa, elongation 5.3 ± 0.4 %, bending modulus 2560 ± 170 MPa, bending strength 55 ± 4 MPa, impact 6.5 ± 0.8 kJ/m²) are not stored. Density, melting, glass transition, Vicat and HDT are raw-material properties (ISO 1183, DSC, ISO 306, ISO 75) and sit under material.* / thermal.*, apart from the printed-specimen mechanical.* rows.

TDS facts with no registry key are not stored: Young's modulus (X-Y 2330 ± 240 MPa, Z 1970 ± 210 MPa), melt index (32.2 ± 4.5 g/10 min at 210 °C, 2.16 kg), crystallization temperature ("/"), heat deflection temperature 56 °C at 0.45 MPa, saturated water absorption rate (0.44 % at 25 °C, 55% RH), printing and storage humidity (< 20% RH, sealed with desiccant), bed surface preparation (glue), retraction length (0.6 - 1.0 mm) and speed (20 - 40 mm/s), chamber temperature (25 - 45 °C), max overhang angle (55 °), max bridging length (30 mm), support material (Support for PLA), spool material (ABS, temperature resistance 70 °C) and spool size (diameter 200 mm, height 67 mm), suggested annealing (50 - 60 °C, 6 - 12 h), odor, skin hazards, chemical stability, solubility, chemical resistance, flammability and combustion products rows.
The TDS recommended chamber temperature (25 - 45 °C) is not written to thermal.chamber_temp: that key is a printer capability (number, template field chamber_temp_max), not a filament print setting.

The TDS "Bed Surface Preparation Glue" is a recommended setting, not a stated requirement, so no "requires" relation is written; the material-table wiki's "Glue Required" applies to the Engineering Plate only and is kept in that relation's note.

SDS facts with no registry key are not stored: model "A07-xx", CLP "Not classified", and "Not hazardous goods" for sea (IMDG), DOT, road (ADR/RID) and air (ICAO/IATA) transport. Its section 9 "No data available" for melting point and density does not override the TDS values.

Source disagreement left to review: bed temperature on the High Temperature and Textured PEI plates (TDS 35 - 45 °C for all three bed types vs material-table wiki 45 - 65 ℃ for "PLA Metal / Wood / Marble"). The product TDS value is kept.

Nozzle guidance disagreement left to review: the material-table wiki row "PLA Marble" says hardened steel is "Not Required", but the guidance under the same table names PLA Marble among particle-filled materials for which a hardened steel nozzle is to be used (0.4 mm hardened steel "highly recommended as the first choice") and stainless steel or brass nozzles avoided; the TDS, the store page and the PLA wiki exclude only the 0.2 mm nozzle.
The material-table wiki note ② says its generic "PLA" rows exclude PLA Marble; only the rows that name Marble ("PLA Marble", "PLA Metal / Wood / Marble") were used for this product.
Marketing prose proves no number: "Natural Stone-like Texture", "Delicate Finish" and "Mimics the Appearance of Natural Stone" (store page) are not stored as values.

Hex: both store colours have exactly one hex cell, matched by the colour name without the code in parentheses (the hex table text layer titles the product "PLA marble"; the rendered page reads "PLA Marble").

The store page links a "Filament RoHS" certificate (https://store.bblcdn.com/1ff1a5ed13714099903ea56349d9a65f.pdf) that was not cached and not read, so safety.certifications is neither curated nor marked not_published.
material.diameter_tolerance (± 0.03 mm) is the store page's own row (Product Features › bullet 3); the TDS gives no tolerance, so it is not restated here and not marked not_published.
No in-the-box list: no official packing list exists for this filament (the store page has no What's in the Box section).
The store FAQ (3.Safety Tips) says the filament "is not food-grade"; no registry key holds it.
